title: Requests and responses
summary: Postman helps inspect HTTP messages. A request asks for work; a response gives a status, headers and sometimes a body.
introduction: Postman helps inspect HTTP messages. A request asks for work; a response gives a status, headers and sometimes a body. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Postman helps inspect HTTP messages. A request asks for work; a response gives a status, headers and sometimes a body.

blocks.title: Before you start
blocks.text: No account or API service is needed to read these examples. practice.test is fictional. Postman scripts require Postman's own environment and do not run in the website playground.
This course teaches the basics. It does not cover every feature of Postman. Keep real personal data and secret keys out of practice files.

blocks.title: Requests and responses

blocks.text: The response describes book 17. This is a worked message, not a request sent by the lesson.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Identify the method, path and response body.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Reading a sample response does not prove a real service will return it.
For more detail later, use this [Postman further reading](https://learning.postman.com/docs/getting-started/overview/).

seo.title: Postman: Requests and responses
